LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 6 schedule, including five locks against the spread Getty Images I don't know what it is about the Week 6 slate, but I think we're going to have some underdogs bark rather loudly. I have four underdogs not only finding their way into my five locks of the week, but also two of them pulling off outright upsets. Judging by the headline of this article, you already know that the Panthers are one of those dogs that I think will win in Week 6 as they head up to Philly to face the Eagles . While I'll get into why I feel that way below, I'm just as fascinated by what may happen if it comes to fruition. Would this be the straw that breaks the camel's back when it comes to Nick Sirianni's job? Or does he live to fight another day and gear up for a do-or-die NFC East showdown in primetime with the Cowboys in Week 7? Either way, the storylines that could flow out of this upcoming slate feel like they're as juicy as we've seen so far this season, and that's saying something. Anyways, I'll look to improve upon my picks after a lackluster Week 5 where I went 2-3 ATS with my five locks of the week, along with 6-9 ATS and 9-5-1 SU for the overall slate. Note : Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6. Locks of the Week ATS : 12-12-1 ATS : 33-44-2 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles Sunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ ) Carolina comes into this matchup with a pretty sizable rest advantage over Philadelphia. On top of the Panthers coming off of the bye, the Eagles were just in London last week. So, we have one team extremely well rested, while the other is reeling and just came off a demoralizing international loss. Beyond the lopsided rest advantage, the Eagles just feel like a mess right now. They're bottom five in the league in points per game (18.4), yards per game (262.2), and passing yards per game (170.6) coming into Week 6. Sure, some of that can be attributed to injury, but even when they've had their full squad, it's been clunky. Conversely, Carolina's offense is top-five in the NFL in those same categories, and it looks like they'll get No. 2 wideout Jalen Coker back for this one. I like the Panthers to roll into Lincoln Financial Field and turn the heat up under Nick Sirianni's seat to a fever pitch. Projected score: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 The pick: Panthers +1.5 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers This is another game that has some outliers worth targeting. The Bucs will be at home after an upset win over the Cowboys last Thursday night in Dallas. They'll have the rest advantage over a Steelers team that took care of business against the Colts on Sunday. Similar to how I think the Cowboys sort of overlooked the then-winless Buccaneers with an undrafted rookie quarterback under center, Pittsburgh could get caught sleeping here, too. Not so much because they're going to overlook Jalon Daniels , but the Steelers could get caught looking ahead to their Week 7 matchup against the Saints in Paris. With a France trip on the horizon for Pittsburgh, I think Tampa Bay is a live home dog. Moreover, I think the Bucs defense has a good shot at containing the Steelers offense. Tampa Bay is allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL through Week 5, which could limit Jaylen Warren's impact. Meanwhile, Todd Bowles has some solid splits against Aaron Rodgers over the course of his career as both a head coach and defensive coordinator. Rodgers' teams are 1-2 against Bowles and average just 16.7 points per game. Projected score: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 23 The pick: Buccaneers +3 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) You'll undoubtedly scratch your head at this pick, and it's hard to blame you. Tennessee hasn't instilled any confidence this season and is punting on a league-high 53% of its drives. Still, I think this line is too big in a divisional matchup against the Colts, whom I don't believe are a serious player in the AFC. The Indy offense can't move the ball efficiently, ranking 29th in the NFL in yards per play (4.6). Meanwhile, their defense is 28th in the league in total yards allowed (384.2). Daniel Jones has also turned the ball over more times (7) than he's found the end zone (4) this season. So, for as bad as the Titans offense has been this season, Indy isn't that far off, so I'll gladly put the full touchdown in my back pocket. Projected score: Colts 24, Titans 20 The pick: Titans +7 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) I think we're firmly on backdoor alert with this line. L.A. is coming off an overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night, so this is quite the turnaround for Sean McVay's club. Matthew Stafford dropped back and threw 54 times in the loss, while the Rams offense ran 78 total plays. That could see them a bit sluggish in this contest. I don't envision Arizona pulling off the upset, but I do think they're capable of scoring late to get us within the number here. For instance, Arizona kept the offense on the field throughout a blowout loss to Detroit and scored a largely meaningless touchdown just before the two-minute warning. That's the type of play we'll be looking for them here. Projected score: Rams 30, Cardinals 17 The pick: Cardinals +13.5 New York Jets at New England Patriots I think the Patriots are all the way back. Drake Maye has seemingly returned to his MVP form from last year and just tallied five touchdowns in a blowout win over the Raiders . Gillette Stadium has been a comfortable spot for New England as they're 10-1 in their last 11 home games. Meanwhile, they've also taken care of business against inferior opponents under Mike Vrabel as the Patriots are 11-0 with him at the helm when facing teams entering with a losing record. Further looking at the trends for this one, the Patriots are 12-0 straight-up and 10-2 ATS in their last 12 games as a favorite and have a +17.9 PPG differential over that stretch. As for the Jets , they've yet to win or cover (0-6) a divisional game under head coach Aaron Glenn. And few teams are more disappointing thus far than the Philadelphia Eagles . Might Nick Sirianni get a pink slip if his club loses at home Sunday against a rested and surging Carolina Panthers team? High 58F. Winds NW at 5 to 10 mph. With the Eagles -1.5 at DraftKings , 94% of ATS handle is on them but 55% of bets are on the Panthers. There's heavy action on the Over with a low total of 40.5. The latest odds I saw post-Week 5 on the first NFL head coach fired had Washington's Dan Quinn as the +200 favorite and Sirianni next at +400. And that's absolutely no surprise to me after both NFC East head coaches made utterly stupid decisions that cost their teams victories this past Sunday. I'm sure you know by know what happened in Commanders-Giants and Eagles-Jaguars. Quinn and/or Jayden Daniels didn't even get a field-goal try off at end of overtime, with a win in Washington's hands. Maybe that clock mistake was on Daniels, but there's no doubt it's on Sirianni for having Jake Elliott kick off into the Jacksonville landing zone on Sunday in London. That allowed a long return and a walk-off 57-yard field goal to win. All the Eagles had to do was kick the ball out of the end zone and the Jags are at their 35 hoping for a Hail Mary with no timeouts. Kudos to Sirianni for taking the blame, but he wouldn't take any for managing the prior scoring drive in a way that left the Jaguars with more time than they should have had. Two passes stopped the clock, and Elliott kicked the go-ahead field goal with 12 seconds left. Why not run it down to only a couple and make that the final play? "I'm honoring a play call, honoring the things that are coming in the game," QB Jalen Hurts said afterward. "We're not asking him to make play calls in that scenario," Sirianni responded to Monday. Starting to feel a disconnect there? The Eagles' next game is on a bit of extra rest, as it is Monday night in Week 7 vs. Dallas, so you might see a change if this goes badly Sunday, even though Sirianni is 67-33 as the Eagles head coach. That's tied for the fifth-best head coaching record through 100 games in the league since 1970. The team's bye isn't until Week 10, and you can already hear the Mike Tomlin rumors. This marks Sirianni's third three-game losing streak in Philadelphia, and he has never lost four in a row. It's not just his clock management, but his offense has been lousy during this skid in averaging 14.7 points and 217 yards per game while converting just 22.2% of third downs. The PPG is the fewest for Philly through five games since 2012, and the YPG the fewest through five since 1999. A juggled offensive line hasn't helped. With Lane Johnson having retired, Cam Jurgens traded and Landon Dickerson on injured reserve, the team has replaced three starters already. And it's not clear yet if the offense will have tailback and former NFL Offensive Player of the Year Saquon Barkley and No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith back from injury yet, after both missed Week 5. The Eagles are averaging a scant 3.5 yards per play with both off the field this season, compared to 5.3 in all other situations. It's possible the Eagles are down to their No. 4 tailback because No. 2 Tank Bigsby is on IR and No. 3 Will Shipley was hurt against the Jags. This will mark the first time the Eagles will take the field sitting below .500 since 2021, when they were 6-7. The 76 straight games played without a losing record was the longest streak in team history. The overall NFL record is 145 by the Patriots from 2003-12. Carolina comes off its bye with its 2-2 mark the team's best four-game start since 2021. It's also good enough for the lead in the ultra-weak NFC South – the Panthers are +130 favorites. We get a former all-Alabama quarterback matchup here in Bryce Young vs. Hurts with Young off to his best start and perhaps answering all those lingering questions that have dogged the former No. 1 overall pick. Thanks to Young and sensational second-year wideout Tetairoa McMillan , the Panthers rank top five in the league in scoring offense (30.3 PPG), total offense (405.8 YPG) and passing offense (301.3 YPG). The scoring average is the best in franchise history through four games, and it's their first time averaging at least 30.0 PPG in any four-game span since 2019. Young would make history if he keeps his NFL-best 317.0-yard passing average up, as no QB ever has averaged even 275 yards passing in a season after three straight years under 200.0 passing yards per. Young also led the NFL entering his bye week with 11 completions on deep throws (20+ air yards). He is 0-1 against Hurts in the NFL as the Eagles beat the visiting Panthers 22-16 in the most recent meeting in December 2024. They're coming off a brilliant upset win over the Detroit Lions, too. The Philadelphia Eagles made the long trek back from London after a mindboggling, crushing defeat where victory was essentially secured. The Panthers have the advantage this week, it seems. Despite that, they're not favored on the road, and some experts aren't willing to pick the Panthers to take the Eagles down. Expert picks for Eagles vs. Panthers in NFL Week 6 action Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni reacts during the first half | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect CBS Sports' Pete Prisco has picked against the Panthers all season, his seeming disdain for the franchise refusing to go away. He isn't changing his ways this week, either, picking the Eagles to win by three despite giving ample reason the Panthers should win. CBS Sports' Pete Prisco has picked against the Panthers all season, his seeming disdain for the franchise refusing to go away. He isn't changing his ways this week, either, picking the Eagles to win by three despite giving ample reason the Panthers should win. "The Panthers are off a bye, while the Eagles are off a trip to London where they lost in brutal fashion to the Jaguars. This is desperation time for the Eagles, but the injuries have piled up. Somehow, though, they will get off the deck to win this behind their defense," he wrote. His CBS colleague, Jordan Dajani, disagreed, picking the Panthers to win 23-21. "The Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS," Dajani pointed out. Here's how SI's staff is picking the game: Albert Breer: Panthers Eva Geitheim: Panthers Mitch Goldich: Eagles Mike Kadlick: Panthers Gilberto Manzano: Panthers Conor Orr: Eagles John Pluym: Eagles Matt Verderame: Eagles Bleacher Report's Wes O'Donnell is taking the Panthers to cover the spread and win outright. "I'm done trying to figure out the Eagles. The Eagles clearly cannot figure out the Eagles. And while the Panthers' defense is a great opportunity for any offense to get right, Carolina had a bye week and then some to prepare for Philly. This Panthers team has defied the odds and shown up in tough situations since last season," he wrote. Carolina Panthers head coach Dave Canales reacts after the game at Bank of America Stadium | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect His colleagues Gary Davenport, Kristopher Knox, Moe Moton, and Brent Sobleski agree, while Ian Hanford and Brad Gagnon disagree, picking the Eagles. His colleagues Gary Davenport, Kristopher Knox, Moe Moton, and Brent Sobleski agree, while Ian Hanford and Brad Gagnon disagree, picking the Eagles. At ESPN , only Pam Maldonado and Dan Graziano picked the Eagles to beat the Panthers. The Athletic's Vic Tafur was obscenely blunt: "The Eagles are coming off two heartbreaking losses, they struggle against play-action passes (a Panthers staple), and it wouldn’t shock me if this is Sirianni’s last game as head coach." What does this mean? Despite the overwhelming advantages the Panthers have in this game, there's still a perception that the Eagles are the Eagles and the Panthers are the woeful Panthers. That makes Week 6's contest a perfect opportunity to reshape the narrative, although it's a little unfair that a primetime victory over the Detroit Lions didn't do that for the Panthers. After escaping with wins against the Commanders and Titans to open the season, the Eagles have lost to the Bears, Rams, and Jaguars. This past week’s loss in London was particularly painful as the Eagles took a 17-16 lead with eight seconds left on the clock before Jacksonville’s kick return and a 57-yard field goal with time expiring. Things went from bad to worse on Thursday with news that Jalen Hurts will be out due to a blood clot. On the flip side, the Panthers are back in action after a bye week and 32-26 upset win against the Lions in their last game. Using the latest odds and analysis, here’s where I’m leaning for this Week 6 matchup with a final score prediction. Panthers vs. Eagles Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Panthers -3.5 (-110) Eagles +3.5 (-110) Panthers: -185 38.5 (Over -108/Under -112) Line Movement: The spread has moved quite a bit since the odds opened for this game. The total has plummeted from 43.5 to 38.5 Panthers vs. Eagles Final Score Prediction SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan broke down this game in his Road to 272 Bets column, in which he picks each game every week: There are very few teams I think the Eagles should be favored against, and the Panthers coming off a BYE week isn't one of them. Not only have the offensive injuries racked up in a major way for Philadelphia, but its numbers continue to be amongst the worst in the NFL. The Eagles are 29th in EPA per play and 24th in opponent EPA per play, putting them in the bottom handful of teams in the entire NFL. They're also dead last in success rate and 22nd in opponent success rate. They've somehow managed to play in close games all season, but unless they fix things in a hurry, they're going to start racking up some ugly losses. Meanwhile, the Panthers' offense is a top-10 unit. They still have some issues on defense, but their offense alone makes me think they should be favored in this NFC matchup. I'll back the Panthers as underdogs on the moneyline. Pick: Panthers +104 via FanDuel The Eagles put everything they had into last week’s game and still came up short. They then had to travel back home from London while the Panthers enjoyed a week off. Carolina isn’t going to take it lightly against the Eagles. Philadelphia will be hungry, but the injuries are piling up, and that’s a bigger deal. The Panthers should win this one, and I’m surprised the total has come down by so many points. away.blurb: "I know what I can do. I genuinely know what I can do. I know the impact I can have on this game," Greenard said on Friday. "I still feel like I'm one of the best at my position. I like myself against anybody. It's just a matter of me getting out there and showing it." The timing of Greenard's return is important as Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) is out and A.J. Epenesa (back) is doubtful. "Our injury report is longer than a novel. It's crazy, man. It's insane," Greenard said. "At the same time, we play a very physically demanding sport. When you're at this point, like we are with the Eagles, you're going to get the best from everybody. You got to make sure you bring it day in and day out. "Nobody is going to come save us, so we have to come get ourselves out of this hole. And we like that. We are not a losing team. We're maybe doing some loser things at times, but we're not a losing team and everybody knows that, so I'm excited to see what we do on Sunday." Wide receiver Hollywood Brown (ankle) and safety Marcus Epps (groin) are also set to return from injury. Center Drew Kendall was limited in practice on both Thursday and Friday. He's questionable for Sunday. The Eagles opened the practice window this week for cornerback Jakorian Bennett (knee), tight end Grant Calcaterra (back), guard Landon Dickerson (knee), and tight end Eli Stowers (knee). All four players are questionable and would have to be activated off Injured Reserve in order to be eligible to play Sunday. It remains to be seen whether the Panthers will activate tackle Taylor Moton (lungs, blood clot) or defensive tackle Tershawn Wharton (neck) from Injured Reserve. Both players were full participants in practice all week, but are officially questionable for Sunday. Moton's potential return would mitigate the likely loss of rookie right tackle Monroe Freeling, who is doubtful with a knee injury. Former Eagle Jaelan Phillips was a full participant in Friday's practice, but the Panthers listed the outside linebacker as questionable with a hamstring injury. home.headline: Eagles turn to former Cowboys QB after Jalen Hurts injury
home.blurb: The Eagles have already ruled Hurts out for their Week 6 contest against the Panthers, but recent reports have indicated he could be out indefinitely. The timing couldn’t be worse with Philadelphia having lost three straight games and sitting under .500 at 2-3. Steelers Make Big Decision on Jaylen Warren Amid Rico Dowdle's Return The Philadelphia Eagles ‘ quarterback room has shifted dramatically over the last couple of days. Franchise star Jalen Hurts has been sidelined with a superficial blood clot in his calf. The issue was reportedly discovered before the Eagles’ game against the Jaguars in Week 5, but doctors initially cleared him to play in Sunday’s game. However, a follow-up ultrasound on Wednesday revealed that the clot had moved. In response, the Eagles have signed quarterback Joe Milton III off the Cowboys’ practice squad, adding him to their 53-man roster just two days before their showdown with Carolina. More news : Raiders Consider Major Decision on Ashton Jeanty Amid Injury Concerns Milton was the Patriots’ sixth-round pick in 2024 after a college career split between Michigan and Tennessee. He’s a physically imposing quarterback at 6-foot-5, 236 pounds, with his biggest selling point being his arm strength, earning him the nickname “Bazooka Joe.” He’s been one of the most exciting young quarterbacks to follow over the last couple of years as a result. However, he hasn’t seen the field much over his first two seasons in the NFL . He’s appeared in just five regular-season games total, one with New England and four with Dallas. Over that span, he’s completed 69.8% of his passes for 424 yards and two touchdowns with two interceptions. He did, however, impress during preseason with the Cowboys this year, throwing for 378 yards and three touchdowns without an interception. Milton has shown an ability to make deep throws and has enough mobility to move around outside the pocket or pick up extra yards with his legs. But he’s not the dual-threat quarterback Hurts was, and it will be hard for Philadelphia to make up for that loss. More news : Chiefs’ Andy Reid Makes Feelings Clear on Kenneth Walker After Explosive Start More news : Wild Cam Ward Stat Makes Bust Debate Impossible to Ignore Milton’s arrival doesn’t automatically make him the starter. Tanner McKee is still expected to start against the Panthers on Sunday. But for Milton, this is a chance to earn a valuable role with a division rival and potentially lock down a bigger contract after the season. The Pittsburgh Steelers are currently 2.5-point favorites for their Week 6 road game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. However, NFL analyst Conor Orr thinks the oddsmakers have it completely wrong. Orr predicts the Steelers will continue their hot streak and dominate the Buccaneers in Week 6. "I wanna see the Steelers go down to Tampa Bay and win another one of these games," Orr said . "I think they can win this game by three touchdowns." Orr has done a complete 180 in just a matter of a week. Heading into Week 5, he begged the Indianapolis Colts to put the Steelers out of their misery. "Clearly you have communication issues. Your coach came out and said your house is dirty and you need to clean your house. Something's a mess here," Orr said on the Heed the Call NFL Podcast . "I'm sick of [Aaron Rodgers]. I'm sick of watching this team. I'm sick of the receivers dropping balls. I'm sick of them having played one good game against the Bengals so we've got to take them seriously for another three weeks. Come on, Jonathan Taylor. Put up 400 yards and put his old, dying horse out of its misery and off my screen." However, after watching the Steelers offense come alive in their latest win, Orr issued an apology to the team and now seems to be a big believer in Pittsburgh. "I have totally done a 180, and I'll admit it, on this Steelers offense," Orr continued. "Down so many people, and even down to Ben Skowronek, this team has been able to find a way to manufacture points. Aaron Rodgers will have bad Rodgers games, but I've totally flipped on this." The Steelers do seem to have some new found life. Rodgers is playing very well and running back Jaylen Warren has been on another level, recording 176, 126 and 188-yard performances the past three weeks. The only question that remains is: Can the Steelers offense continue this type of production the rest of the season? away.headline: Pittsburgh Steelers get big Baker Mayfield news before Buccaneers game
away.blurb: The Pittsburgh Steelers will not see Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield this week, as he will miss another week after suffering a dislocated thumb. Mayfield is targeting a Week 7 return, but it will instead be undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels getting his third straight start. Daniels was able to play in a positive game script with the running game going, and the Buccaneers offensive line allowed the third lowest pressure rate of the week. The rookie out of Kansas was pressured on just 29.3 percent of his drop backs. Daniels has 337 yards, two passing touchdowns, and three interceptions while completing 69.1 percent of his attempts thus far on the year. He earned his first career win as a starting NFL quarterback by helping knock off the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football last week. The Steelers have prepared for Daniels, not Mayfield, all week with the former Oklahoma product not practicing as he still does physical therapy to help him grip a football better. For now, Daniels’ elusiveness and mobility will be the focus for the Steelers. “We have to be disciplined in our rush lanes,” outside linebacker Alex Highsmith said. “Up front, we can’t rush scared. We have to rush like we always rush, but we have to trace back to the quarterback and not give him lanes to escape. He’s dynamic and has a really good arm, so we have to be ready.” In order for the Steelers to win, they will have to contain Daniels and force him into bad situations. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. away.headline: Steelers’ rookies stepping up for injured starters
away.blurb: Fellow former SEC products in Georgia's Daylen Everette and Oklahoma's Robert Spears-Jennings have stood out on the defensive side of the ball. Everette forced two pass breakups in the win, one of them to Colts wide receiver Deion Burks. The thing that stands out to me is the physicality, whether it's in the coverage, whether it's in the tackling; that's what I'm pleased to see from a young corner, because again, the run game, we all know this in this league," Steelers' defensive coordinator Patrick Graham said. "At some point, they're trying to get the ball out to the corners and for him to show up." With safety DeShon Elliott being out for the first five weeks, Spears-Jennings has played a critical role in the secondary. Not only does he have one interception to his name, but he has been a catalyst for the defense's communication. "That's what you want out of a secondary guy that, you know, that's just going to communicate every single place and got your back on to come down, lay WOOD every single time. So definitely love him back there," Steelers linebacker Patrick Queen said. "You're trying to earn the respect of your your teammates to show that they can rely upon you when you're out there on the field or rely on you when you're out there on the field," Graham added. "And he does that by his play, by correcting himself after making a mistake. And he's very detailed." "But you know, I do agree with you. I think we're off to a good start there because we're playing you know, they're playing early." One of the more prominent rookies is wide receiver Germie Bernard. The Alabama product caught six passes for 80 yards in his largest role to date. He will have a bigger part in the offense with the absence of receivers Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek. away.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have released their final injury report ahead of Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and several key players will be unavailable as Tampa Bay looks to build on last week's victory over Dallas. Quarterback Baker Mayfield (right thumb) has officially been ruled out after missing all three practices this week. Rookie Jalon Daniels will make his third consecutive start after leading the Buccaneers to their first victory of the season last Thursday against the Cowboys. The Buccaneers will also be without safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib), who did not participate in practice throughout the week. Wide receiver David Sills V (hamstring) was also ruled out despite being listed as a full participant in all three practices. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison (quad) is listed as doubtful, while linebackers SirVocea Dennis (ankle/foot) and Josiah Trotter (knee), cornerback Ayden Garnes (ankle), and running back Sean Tucker (quad) are questionable. Dennis and Garnes were full participants Friday, providing some encouraging news heading into the weekend. Pittsburgh is also dealing with several injuries, particularly at wide receiver. Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) have been ruled out, along with safety DeShon Elliott (knee). Wide receiver DK Metcalf was added to Friday's report with an illness and is questionable. away.headline: Steelers injury report: Pittsburgh enters road trip with abundance of injuries
away.blurb: Out of the bye, road trips to face the division rival Bengals and in-state rival Eagles await. Neither is a long trip in terms of mileage, but the Steelers have not won in Philadelphia since 1965, and it follows an AFC North dogfight. The receivers room is the most pressing problem. Pittman will be out for at least the next three games after being placed on injured reserve. The veteran was a key offseason acquisition but has only played in three games in which he’s caught seven passes for 89 yards. The extent of the injuries to Wilson and Skowronek, sustained against Indianapolis, are not yet known, but McCarthy said Monday that both will be out for at least the Tampa Bay game. The secondary is a bit better off. Ramsey spent the week leading up to the Colts game on the injury report but handled a normal workload. Only Dean was absent, and the Steelers have not yet taken the step of adding the free agent cornerback signing to injured reserve. Dean was a limited practice participant Wednesday while Ramsey was out with a wrist injury listed. McCarthy hinted strongly that Dowdle is expected back this week from the toe injury he sustained in Week 2 against New England. He was also limited Wednesday. That should help the offense manage the reps of Jaylen Warren, who’s handled a heavy workload in Dowdle’s absence. First-year coach Mike McCarthy’s team will play four of its next five games on the road starting this week, and it will take multiple longer – and daunting – trips to do so before things begin to moderate in the back half of the 2026 schedule. All of it will unfold amid mounting absences. Running back Rico Dowdle; receivers Michael Pittman Jr., Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek; and defensive backs Jamel Dean and Jalen Ramsey have all been hurt in some form or fashion recently. The stretch will be one of, if not the, most grueling in the franchise’s history and could determine whether the Steelers ’ 3-2 start has legs, or whether another mediocre year awaits a franchise that hasn’t won an NFL playoff game since 2017. NFL Week 6 brings a road trip to Tampa Bay to face the Buccaneers . That’s a 1,000-or-so-mile trip right off the bat against a desperate 1-4 team that needs a win to preserve any postseason hopes. One week later, the Steelers will board a long flight to Paris to face the New Orleans Saints in the first NFL regular season game in France. It will be only the second international game for Pittsburgh since 2013. It picked up a win against Minnesota in Dublin, Ireland last October, but the travel schedule was much kinder surrounding that date. home.headline: Buccaneers Have Return Date in Mind for QB Baker Mayfield: Report
home.blurb: Buccaneers Have Return Date in Mind for QB Baker Mayfield: Report The Tampa Bay Buccaneers will start undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels for a third consecutive game in Week 6 when they return home to face the Pittsburgh Steelers. "Bucs QB Baker Mayfield will miss a third consecutive game since dislocating his thumb in Week 3," Pelissero wrote on his official X account on Saturday morning. "But there's optimism he'll return next week — just in time for Tampa Bay's first division game of the season at Carolina." The Buccaneers aren't taking any chances on Mayfield's recovery. He got the stitches out of his thumb last week and tried to throw early this week, which led the Bucs to quickly rule him out against the Steelers. Daniels' play has also been a big reason Mayfield's return hasn't been rushed. Unlock the latest Heavy on Buccaneers news — direct to your inbox. Updated Oct 17, 2026 at 10:50am According to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero , the Buccaneers believe this could be Daniels' final start before $165 million quarterback Baker Mayfield returns from a thumb injury for a critical Week 7 game against the Carolina Panthers . Bucs Determined Mayfield's Status Early in Week "Baker Mayfield is NOT practicing today so we can stop speculating," Tampa Bay Times NFL reporter Rick Stround wrote on his official X account on October 15. "Jalon Daniels will start vs the Steelers barring something unforeseen." "Baker Mayfield working his way back but not there yet," NFL Network's Mike Garafolo wrote on his official X account. "It'll be Jalon Daniels against the Steelers ." "Another week as the starter for Jalon Daniels," NFL Network's Ian Rapoport wrote on his official X account. Jalon Daniels Led Buccaneers to First Win Daniels is 1-1 as Tampa Bay's starter since Mayfield hurt his thumb in the fourth quarter of a Week 3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings , and the win over the Cowboys lifted the Buccaneers to 1-4 on the season. It's a win that may have saved Tampa Bay's season. "Since QB starts were first tracked in 1950, only one QB has done the following in each of his first 2 NFL starts: completed 70% of his passes thrown, a TD pass, and rushed for 20+ yards," OptaStats wrote on its official X account on Thursday night. "That one QB is Jalon Daniels. He was undrafted." Daniels also did something against the Cowboys that no one had done in almost 40 years. "Jalon Daniels is the first undrafted rookie starting QB to beat the Cowboys since 1987 (Washington's Ed Rubbert)," ESPN Insights wrote on its official X account. Daniels went 19-of-25 for 189 yards, 1 touchdown, and no interceptions in the win over the Cowboys, plus 23 rushing yards. He was making his 2nd consecutive start after Baker Mayfield hurt his thumb in Week 3. "Jalon Daniels picked up his first career QB win against the Cowboys on TNF, becoming the fifth undrafted rookie quarterback in the Common Draft Era to win a primetime game," the NFL wrote on its official X account. home.headline: Buccaneers vs. Steelers: Final injury report for Week 6
home.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have released their final injury report ahead of Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and several key players will be unavailable as Tampa Bay looks to build on last week's victory over Dallas. Quarterback Baker Mayfield (right thumb) has officially been ruled out after missing all three practices this week. Rookie Jalon Daniels will make his third consecutive start after leading the Buccaneers to their first victory of the season last Thursday against the Cowboys. The Buccaneers will also be without safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib), who did not participate in practice throughout the week. Wide receiver David Sills V (hamstring) was also ruled out despite being listed as a full participant in all three practices. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison (quad) is listed as doubtful, while linebackers SirVocea Dennis (ankle/foot) and Josiah Trotter (knee), cornerback Ayden Garnes (ankle), and running back Sean Tucker (quad) are questionable. Dennis and Garnes were full participants Friday, providing some encouraging news heading into the weekend. Pittsburgh is also dealing with several injuries, particularly at wide receiver. Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) have been ruled out, along with safety DeShon Elliott (knee). Wide receiver DK Metcalf was added to Friday's report with an illness and is questionable. home.headline: Steelers Injury Central: 3 Out, 5 Questionable vs. Buccaneers
home.blurb: Steelers Injury Central: 3 Out, 5 Questionable vs. Buccaneers Opens in a new tab Steelers News Three Pittsburgh Steelers have been ruled out for the team's Week 6 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, and five more are questionable to suit up, according to the team's Friday injury report. Two wide receivers Ben Skowronek and Roman Wilson left the team's 34-22 Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts with injures and did not return — and they won't be back next week, either. Skowronek suffered a calf injury early in the second quarter, and then Wilson injured his left hand on the final offensive drive of the first half. Wilson had a large wrap on his left hand after the game. On Monday, head coach Mike McCarthy said neither player will return to active this week. Fellow wide receiver DK Metcalf is questionable to play after missing practice on Friday with an illness. Strong safety DeShon Elliott remains limited in practice and will not return this week. Starting cornerback Jamel Dean was ruled out last week, but might be ahead of the curve on the initial multi-week estimate for his injury. He is listed as questionable. Running back Rico Dowdle , who is recovering from a dislocated toe on his left foot, is also questionable to make his return to the lineup, as is defensive tackle Keeanu Benton , who has an ankle injury, and defensive back Jalen Ramsey , who has played through his broken wrist the last two weeks. Wide receiver DK Metcalf missed practice on Friday, Oct. 16 with an illness and has been listed as questionable to play in the Steelers' Week 6 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. With three other wide receivers already ruled out, the Steelers would likely move veteran Isaiah Hodgins or Brandon Johnson into the staring lineup from the practice squad if Metcalf is unable to play. Running back Rico Dowdle was a full participant in practice on Thursday, Oct. 15 and Friday, Oct. 16, but remains questionable to return to the lineup on Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He had been a limited participant in practice for the fourth straight session on Wednesday, Oct. 14. Dowdle did not play in Week 5 after being listed as questionable. He was limited in all three sessions leading up to the week. Dowdle did not play in the Steelers' Week 4 game against the Cleveland Browns after missing all three practice session of the week. He was also ruled out of the Steelers' Week 3 game against the Cincinnati Bengals. Dowdle suffered the toe injury in the Steelers' Week 2 loss to the New England Patriots . He initially left the game, and was listed as questionable, before attempting to return. But Dowdle eventually exited again and was ruled out. Defensive tackle Keeanu Benton was a full participant in practice on Friday, Oct. 16, but remains questionable to play on Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Brown coming off IR ALCS Game 4 postponed Defense will win WNBA Finals Behind Enemy Lines: Previewing Rams-Cardinals with expert Q&A Cameron DaSilva, Rams Wire Sat, October 17, 2026 at 12:01 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Los Angeles Rams have their second divisional matchup of the season this weekend, as they'll host the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday afternoon. It's their first meeting with Mike LaFleur's team after he spent the last three years as Sean McVay's offensive coordinator. To preview this NFC West matchup, we asked Cards Wire lead writer Jess Root five questions, even getting his final score prediction (spoiler: he expects the Rams to win big). Do the Cardinals have anyone on offense who can beat the Rams besides Trey McBride and Michael Wilson? Cards Wire: The short answer is no, but other guys will make a few plays. Teagan Quitoriano scored twice last week (his first touchdowns since 2022). Elijah Higgins will be open more as McBride is getting a lot of attention. Kendrick Bourne is reliable. However, none of those guys are players that can be leaned upon for big plays or critical moments. How big of a blow is Jeremiyah Love's injury? Cards Wire: Well, he hadn't been given the offense much overall, but the absence of his skillset will make the running game less dynamic. Tyler Allgeier is certainly capable and Bam Knight has had moments for the Cardinals, but Love's absence makes an anemic running game look even less threatening. Is it still too early for the Cardinals to turn to Carson Beck? Cards Wire: That is the big debate right now. While Jacoby Brissett hasn't been the problem, he hasn't been good, and after going 2-15 in 17 starts for the Cardinals, he doesn't have much of a ceiling. However, the Cardinals gave him a big raise before the season, so they will keep rolling him out until he isn't best option for them. Many want to see Beck, but with only one start in the preseason, no one knows if he is ready or not. What are the early reviews of Mike LaFleur as a head coach? Cards Wire: They are mixed. He sounded good early on, and the offense has had more overall production than last season. However, the defense is terrible. He has become a little less transparent in his answers, and the offense really has been unimpressive with almost no big plays. Who wins on Sunday and what's the final score? Cards Wire: Considering the Cardinals' struggles defensively and against the NFC West, it's a blowout with late offense from the Cardinals. away.headline: Mike LaFleur is dreaming of man coverage: 4 things Rams fans should know about the Cardinals
away.blurb: The Arizona Cardinals team visiting the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday is lighter at wide receiver than the one Los Angeles swept last season. Arizona traded Marvin Harrison Jr. to Houston during Week 5, and rookie running back Jeremiyah Love is ruled out with an ankle injury . What’s left is a 1-4 team sliding in the power rankings and searching for an identity. Here are four things Rams fans should know before the 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff in Inglewood. Harrison trade puts the focus on man coverage With Harrison gone, Mike LaFleur wants his receivers hunting one-on-ones. “You dream of man coverage. You can’t wait for man coverage,” LaFleur told the Cardinals team website . “It’s me versus you, I don’t care who you are or what the name is on the back of your jersey, I am going to beat you.” The Giants played man 56% of the time in Week 4 and the Lions 51% in Week 5, and neither Trey McBride nor Michael Wilson is averaging six yards per target, as we covered when LaFleur talked man coverage . McBride is ready for the attention. “I expect them to double me,” he said. Arizona had five plays of 20-plus yards through four games, a number Bleacher Report’s Brad Gagnon called “easily the worst mark in the NFL,” which dragged LaFleur to a C+ quarter-season grade . Harrison’s exit doesn’t add speed to an offense that ranks dead last in big plays . Love’s absence takes away another option. Tyler Allgeier starts, and LaFleur said of Love’s ankle, “When he puts his left foot in the ground, it’s just not right right now,” per the team website . Defense giving up 30-plus every week Arizona ranks last in the league at 32.4 points allowed per game, per Pro Football Reference , and has allowed at least 30 in four straight losses. LaFleur still kept Nick Rallis in charge of the defense after the 45-21 loss to Detroit. Fans noticed. Some Cardinals fans have gone as far as taking their frustration to billboards , and a trip to face the league’s top-yardage offense is a rough spot to turn it around. Arizona’s sack leader is a safety. Budda Baker has 2.5 of the team’s 11 sacks and 36 tackles, per his Pro Football Reference page , and he’s the only Cardinal with more than one sack. That tells you how little heat the front generates. Arizona pressures the quarterback on 30.3% of dropbacks, the second-lowest rate in the league, per Rams On SI . Matthew Stafford should have time, even with David Quessenberry filling in at left tackle. away.headline: Arizona Cardinals' LaFleur announces Jeremiyah Love injury status
away.blurb: It is not yet clear whether Love’s injury will affect his availability in Week 7, when the Cardinals return home to face the Denver Broncos. When asked whether Love could be placed on injured reserve, LaFleur said “there’s been no discussion of IR or anything like that.” “He's doing good but it's just — you guys see the way he cuts,” LaFleur said. “He cuts hard. That's a superpower of his. And when he's putting his left foot in the ground, it's just not right, right now. And to get him to be to his best ability, it's what's right so he can go out and perform the way that he wants.” Earlier in the week, LaFleur said that Love’s limited involvement as a receiver was because the Cardinals needed their running backs to stay back in pass protection against the Lions. On Friday, he acknowledged that was only a partial truth. Amid a slow start to his rookie season, Love will miss the Arizona Cardinals ' Week 6 trip to face the Los Angeles Rams due to an injury to his left ankle, head coach Mike LaFleur said on Friday, Oct. 16. Love has not practiced all week after experiencing lingering discomfort in recent games. “We knew on Monday after watching the game, talking with him, seeing where he was at, that we were gonna give him Wednesday off,” LaFleur said. “And re-assess on Wednesday, with knowing that probably Sunday was a long shot.” “We've gotta really re-evaluate, really every single day,” LaFleur added. “Not good enough, obviously, right now to go Sunday. It wouldn't be in the best interest of him. And then we'll re-evaluate, obviously, on Monday.” Love suffered a high-ankle sprain to his right ankle on Aug. 13, in a preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders. He returned to the field a month later in the Cardinals’ regular-season opener. Then, at some point in the ensuing weeks, he began to experience discomfort in his left ankle. The issue first drew public attention in Week 4, against the New York Giants. During that game, trainers repeatedly looked at Love’s ankle on the Cardinals sideline. Afterward, Love acknowledged that the Cardinals have been managing his workload due to health. LaFleur, though, was unsure of exactly when the issue first surfaced. "We just felt like it wasn't improving and maybe even getting a little bit worse," LaFleur said. "So at that point, if it's not improving and it's getting a little bit worse, we've gotta do what's right for the player." Through five games, Love has just 245 rushing yards on 67 carries, for a 3.7 yards per carry average. Love has also caught just 11 passes on 14 targets for 36 yards, falling far short of the expectations with he entered the NFL as a pass-catcher. Over the Cardinals’ past two games, he ran just 20 total routes. “To run routes and separate, you've gotta be able to put those feet in the ground,” LaFleur said. “And it's gotta be deliberate. Recovered from the right high-ankle sprain suffered in the Aug. 13 preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders , his left ankle has been an issue for several weeks. home.headline: Mike LaFleur is dreaming of man coverage: 4 things Rams fans should know about the Cardinals
home.blurb: The Arizona Cardinals team visiting the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday is lighter at wide receiver than the one Los Angeles swept last season. Arizona traded Marvin Harrison Jr. to Houston during Week 5, and rookie running back Jeremiyah Love is ruled out with an ankle injury . What’s left is a 1-4 team sliding in the power rankings and searching for an identity. Here are four things Rams fans should know before the 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff in Inglewood. Harrison trade puts the focus on man coverage With Harrison gone, Mike LaFleur wants his receivers hunting one-on-ones. “You dream of man coverage. You can’t wait for man coverage,” LaFleur told the Cardinals team website . “It’s me versus you, I don’t care who you are or what the name is on the back of your jersey, I am going to beat you.” The Giants played man 56% of the time in Week 4 and the Lions 51% in Week 5, and neither Trey McBride nor Michael Wilson is averaging six yards per target, as we covered when LaFleur talked man coverage . McBride is ready for the attention. “I expect them to double me,” he said. Arizona had five plays of 20-plus yards through four games, a number Bleacher Report’s Brad Gagnon called “easily the worst mark in the NFL,” which dragged LaFleur to a C+ quarter-season grade . Harrison’s exit doesn’t add speed to an offense that ranks dead last in big plays . Love’s absence takes away another option. Tyler Allgeier starts, and LaFleur said of Love’s ankle, “When he puts his left foot in the ground, it’s just not right right now,” per the team website . Defense giving up 30-plus every week Arizona ranks last in the league at 32.4 points allowed per game, per Pro Football Reference , and has allowed at least 30 in four straight losses. LaFleur still kept Nick Rallis in charge of the defense after the 45-21 loss to Detroit. Fans noticed. Some Cardinals fans have gone as far as taking their frustration to billboards , and a trip to face the league’s top-yardage offense is a rough spot to turn it around. Arizona’s sack leader is a safety. Budda Baker has 2.5 of the team’s 11 sacks and 36 tackles, per his Pro Football Reference page , and he’s the only Cardinal with more than one sack. That tells you how little heat the front generates. Arizona pressures the quarterback on 30.3% of dropbacks, the second-lowest rate in the league, per Rams On SI . Matthew Stafford should have time, even with David Quessenberry filling in at left tackle. home.headline: Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams
home.blurb: TEMPE — The Arizona Cardinals are holding star rookie running back Jeremiyah Love out of practice on Wednesday as Week 6 preperations for the Los Angeles Rams ramp up. Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams Skip to main content SI.COM "Take him one day at a time. You know, we want to get this ankle right and do it the right way," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters on Wednesday. Love has been nursing an ankle injury through the opening stages of his rookie season after suffering a different ankle injury during preseason. While he hasn't missed any regular season action, Love's participation and impact has been slightly hindered. There's been some talks about potentially shutting Love down to allow the ankle to heal, though LaFleur didn't seem willing to do that. Arizona is just 1-4 and is again favored to lose in Los Angeles. "Listen, I'm going to try to be as candid as possible with also knowing that everyone's listening to this too, right? But he's a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. I mean, imagine being a running back in the NFL trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you know that you're capable of," LaFleur said. "And so we all are in agreeance — as much as you know he wants to battle through — we're all in agreeance right now, it's just hey, give [the injury] a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on, what that'll entail for Sunday." Love, the No. 3 overall pick, has 67 carries for 245 yards and one touchdown on the ground while adding 11 receptions for 36 yards and a score through the air. "I think early at his career [he battled injuries], but you had the right [ankle] early, and then now you got the left one. So now you're just kind of — it's just double dipping. The right side, the preseason one's fine. It's the other one right now that's the lingering issue. They're ankles, you know, it's an ankle. I'm not a doctor, and each body's a little bit different," LaFleur continued. "Like the way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable, like he doesn't even feel it. But this one is the one that happened kind of when the regular season started, and it just lingered." Has Love lost any of his explosiveness? "You'd have to ask him that," LaFleur added. "I know how explosive he is. I know how explosive he wants to be. So I mean I think that's a fair assessment in some aspects. Again, I don't think it's an overall hindrance, but again the the rest for him is going to be vital." Kansas City is 4-0 after its bye, while Los Angeles is 0-5 following a 23-17 loss to Denver. Kickoff at Arrowhead Stadium is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET. The Chiefs are favored by 8.5 points, but a routine favorite winning comfortably would hardly qualify as a bold prediction. Instead, this forecast projects an exceptional rushing performance, an unexpected Chargers defensive highlight and a fourth-quarter rally that changes the complexion of the afternoon without changing the winner. Kenneth Walker III rushes for 200 yards and three touchdowns Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images Walker has already accumulated 537 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 87 carries through four games. That translates to more than six yards per attempt, giving Kansas City a foundation for dominating without asking Patrick Mahomes to carry every possession. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Chiefs average 6.5 yards per offensive play compared with the Chargers' 4.8. Their third-down conversion rate is also substantially better: 44% against 34.85%. Those advantages can sustain drives and produce the repeated rushing opportunities necessary for a monster individual afternoon. The prediction goes beyond another efficient outing. Walker reaches 200 rushing yards for the game and scores three times, becoming the central reason Kansas City controls possession and repeatedly finishes drives. There is an important limitation: Los Angeles allows only 5.0 yards per play, the same figure as Kansas City. This is not a forecast built on pretending the Chargers cannot defend. It depends on Walker maintaining his explosiveness while the Chiefs create an unusually favorable game script. If Kansas City builds an early advantage, sustained rushing volume can turn Walker's strong start into the biggest performance of his season. The Chargers intercept Patrick Mahomes twice, including a pick-six Mahomes has thrown nine touchdown passes against two interceptions through four games, with a 106.2 passer rating. Predicting two interceptions in one afternoon means Los Angeles matches his entire season total, despite entering winless. The statistical route to that surprise exists. The Chargers allow opponents to convert just 31.25% of third downs, compared with Kansas City's 37.04%. Forcing longer, obvious passing situations could provide opportunities that disappear when Walker keeps the offense ahead of schedule. Los Angeles needs more than ordinary defensive stops because its offense averages just 16.8 points per game. A defensive touchdown would change both field position and scoreboard pressure without requiring Justin Herbert to repeatedly rescue stalled possessions. The call is that one aggressive coverage read becomes an interception return for a touchdown, while another takeaway interrupts a promising Chiefs drive. That would be an unexpected blemish on Mahomes' efficient opening month. It would also illustrate why a team's record does not eliminate its capacity to produce a game-changing individual moment. Justin Herbert leads a 17-point fourth quarter, but Kansas City survives Herbert's current numbers make this the most counterintuitive offensive prediction: 937 passing yards, five touchdowns, seven interceptions and a 70.2 passer rating through five games. He has also absorbed 17 sacks. Against Denver, he managed 121 passing yards and was sacked five times. Receiving availability remains uncertain after Ladd McConkey dressed without playing, Quentin Johnston missed the game and Tre' Harris suffered a hamstring injury. Nevertheless, the prediction is that Herbert finally finds rhythm against a defense protecting a substantial lead. Two touchdown drives and a field goal produce 17 fourth-quarter points, forcing Kansas City to finish the game with its offense rather than coast. Walker provides that answer. The final forecast is Chiefs 38, Chargers 31: Kansas City remains unbeaten, but Los Angeles delivers a much stronger response than its record suggests. These are deliberately high-variance predictions, not the most likely outcomes. The underlying numbers favor Kansas City, but divisional familiarity and turnovers can make a comfortable matchup unpredictable. It's a classic example of an unstoppable force versus an immovable object: an unbeaten Chiefs team hosting a winless Los Angeles squad desperate for answers. KC is among the favorites in the AFC to reach the Super Bowl in early projections. Patrick Mahomes is back to his MVP form after tearing his ACL against this same Chargers team a year ago, and the addition of running back Kenneth Walker has transformed the offense into a juggernaut. Can LA turn its campaign around and pull off an upset in Arrowhead Stadium this weekend? Let's take a look at what ESPN's Matchup Predictor says heading into kickoff. Chargers at Chiefs: ESPN Matchup Predictor Gives Prediction Justin Herbert and Mahomes have had some great battles over the years, though this matchup comes under unusual circumstances. The Chargers haven't started a season 0-5 since the team was still based in San Diego more than 20 years ago. Despite their dismal record, the Chargers still have a decent chance of coming out on top Sunday, according to the matchup predictor. For context, before the bye, the computer model only gave the Chiefs a 3.5% greater chance of beating an undefeated Raiders team on the road. Chiefs on SI's Take The Chargers are far out of the divisional race and likely out of playoff contention, but Jim Harbaugh's squad isn't as awful as its start suggests. It's hard to imagine a team of this caliber finishing with just four or five wins. LA suffered inexplicable defeats to the Raiders and Cardinals early in the season. Just when they appeared poised to finally get into the win column last week, the Chargers collapsed in the fourth quarter against fellow AFC West opponent, the Denver Broncos. The matchup predictor gives the Chargers better than a one-in-four chance against KC, suggesting a win may not be too far off the radar for Los Angeles, whether it comes this week or next. The Chargers can't head into November without a single victory... right? That means the offense will lean heavily on Walker and Travis Kelce to carry the load. If the Chargers are going to put up a fight, Herbert has to pick up his play - point-blank, period. It's been a humiliating stretch for someone who is usually considered one of the AFC's best signal-callers, as he's thrown seven interceptions to his five touchdowns in 2026. away.headline: Chargers get major Ladd McConkey injury update before Chiefs game
away.blurb: Wide receiver Ladd McConkey has no injury designation for Sunday’s game, clearing the way for his expected return after dealing with a lingering foot injury. ESPN’s Adam Schefter confirmed the development Friday, citing the Chargers’ final injury report. The announcement comes after McConkey was limited during practice Wednesday and Thursday while continuing to recover from an injury that has affected his availability in recent weeks. McConkey was listed as questionable ahead of last Sunday’s matchup against the Denver Broncos. Although he was active for the game, the receiver did not play a single offensive snap. McConkey’s return could provide a much-needed boost to quarterback Justin Herbert and a Chargers passing attack that has struggled to establish consistency. While McConkey has been cleared to play, it remains unclear whether he will immediately return to his usual workload after dealing with a lingering foot injury. The Los Angeles Chargers received encouraging news Friday as they prepare for an important AFC West matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs. Los Angeles ultimately suffered a 23-17 loss, continuing a difficult start to the season. Through four appearances this season, McConkey has recorded 12 receptions for 183 yards and one touchdown. Those numbers represent a disappointing start for a receiver who established himself as one of Herbert’s most reliable targets during his first two NFL seasons. However, injuries have played a significant role in limiting his opportunities. The Chargers have also dealt with health concerns involving several other receivers, including Quentin Johnston, Tre’ Harris and Brenen Thompson. Johnston has been managing a chest injury, while Harris suffered a hamstring injury during the loss to Denver. Those setbacks have created additional challenges for Herbert, who has been forced to navigate an offense dealing with injuries at multiple positions. Now, Los Angeles faces another difficult test against Kansas City. Sunday’s matchup against Kansas City presents another challenge for a Chargers team looking to gain momentum in the AFC West. McConkey’s availability gives Justin Herbert a reliable target in the passing game and could provide a much-needed boost to an offense that has struggled with injuries. The Chargers will have to determine how heavily to involve him after his recent injury struggles. For now, Friday’s announcement represents a positive development as Los Angeles prepares to face one of its biggest division rivals. away.blurb: Included in the list of injured players were starting left tackle Joe Alt (neck, DNP), star safety Derwin James Jr. (hamstring, DNP) and leading wide receivers Ladd McConkey (foot, limited participant) and Quentin Johnston (chest, limited). At wide receiver, Los Angeles is dealing with a plethora of issues. (KCTV) - A wounded and winless Los Angeles Chargers team is headed toward Kansas City this weekend looking to hand the Chiefs their first loss of the season. But those aforementioned wounds are mounting after five weeks of play, and Wednesday’s injury report shared by head coach Jim Harbaugh’s team was a lengthy one. In total, nearly 40 percent of the Chargers’ active roster were listed with some ailment after their first practice of the week. Not included on the injury report was Chargers center Tyler Biadasz, who was placed on season-ending injured reserve in August due to a torn ACL suffered in training camp and starting right tackle Rashawn Slater and backup Trey Pipkins, who were each placed on injured reserve in recent weeks due to ankle and knee issues. As a result, last week, injuries on the Chargers offensive line led to multiple rookies starting for Los Angeles in a game where star quarterback Justin Herbert was sacked five times. All of those injuries to Chargers pass-catchers, which include tight end David Njoku being placed on injured reserve in September, resulted in the Chargers hosting several wide receivers for tryouts on Tuesday and signing former Raymore-Peculiar and KU alum Luke Grimm to their practice squad. Kansas City and Los Angeles kick off Sunday’s game at 3:25 p.m. CT. It can be watched live in Kansas City and the surrounding viewing area on KCTV5.

home.headline: Latest Tyreek Hill Rumors on Concerns About Injury and Contract amid Chiefs Buzz
home.blurb: While Hill has been linked to a return to the Kansas City Chiefs since he spent his first six seasons with the organization and could potentially help their injury-ravaged receiving corps, Jones noted that he does not "get the sense" the Chiefs are "in a rush" to sign him. His strong play carried over to his tenure with the Miami Dolphins, as he was a Pro Bowler and First Team All-Pro in each of his first two seasons in Miami before injuries hampered his effectiveness in 2024 and limited him to four games in 2025. It is already known that he has on-field chemistry with Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, but there is no indication that his return to Kansas City is a sure thing. The Chiefs will likely be without wide receiver Tyquan Thornton for the rest of the regular season , and No. 1 wideout Rashee Rice is out this week with a hamstring injury . However, Hill has looked more explosive in subsequent videos, and his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said during an appearance on the Pat McAfee Show (h/t Kyle Dvorchak of NBC Sports) last month that multiple teams had expressed interest in Hill and that he could return to action "perhaps some time in October." Should the injuries continue to mount, there may not be a better option available to them, particularly one who knows and understands head coach Andy Reid's offense like Hill does. The Las Vegas Raiders received encouraging news regarding Ashton Jeanty's health as the team prepares for Sunday's matchup against the Buffalo Bills. After spending much of the season dealing with foot and ankle injuries, the second-year running back appears to be making significant progress. Speaking with reporters at his locker Thursday, Jeanty said he was feeling great and that this was the best he had felt all season, according to ESPN reporter Ryan McFadden. Jeanty appeared to aggravate the ankle during Las Vegas' Week 4 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs before dealing with an additional foot issue ahead of last Sunday's matchup against the New England Patriots.

The Las Vegas Raiders received encouraging news regarding Ashton Jeanty's health as the team prepares for Sunday's matchup against the Buffalo Bills. After spending much of the season dealing with foot and ankle injuries, the second-year running back appears to be making significant progress. Speaking with reporters at his locker Thursday, Jeanty said he was feeling great and that this was the best he had felt all season, according to ESPN reporter Ryan McFadden. "He's playing," Kubiak said when asked about potentially sitting Jeanty. Kubiak also noted that Jeanty was making progress in his recovery, raising the possibility that he could take on a larger workload during practice. Jeanty's comments Thursday offered further encouragement, suggesting that the running back is beginning to feel more comfortable after battling injuries throughout the season. The former Boise State standout first suffered an ankle injury during training camp in August. While he recovered in time for the regular season, the issue has continued to linger, making it difficult for him to play at full strength. Jeanty appeared to aggravate the ankle during Las Vegas' Week 4 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs before dealing with an additional foot issue ahead of last Sunday's matchup against the New England Patriots.

NFL teams have to submit a report on practice participation on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday for a Sunday game. Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was going to happen. The "weird" came in the form of a 31-7 beatdown of Tyson Bagent . It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. Now, they have to go to Lambeau Field and try to stop a quarterback in Jordan Love , who is clearly finding his rhythm, having just thrown for 367 yards and two touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are definitely a fun duo, but so are Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft . … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24 Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. Dallas should put up points, too, because the Packers' defense is no great shakes, but I'm taking Green Bay to win here. … Prediction: Packers 33, Cowboys 28 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) (MNF) Dajani (49ers -7.5): I am genuinely curious how the Commanders running the clock out on themselves affected the locker room.
