Stroud, Green Bay gets its ground game rolling against Dallas, and Justin Herbert breaks out of an ugly slump Getty Images Anything can happen in the NFL , and the start to Week 6 of the 2026 season certainly hammered home that fact. In the Denver Broncos (4-2) 17-14 "Thursday Night Football" overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks , they triumphed at home despite averaging 2.9 yards per play. That's the fewest in Sean Payton's 318-game head-coaching career, and Denver's 168 total yards of offense ranked as their fewest in a victory since Pro Football Hall of Fame quarterback John Elway's first start as a rookie in 1983. Quarterback Bo Nix , who ranks dead last in the NFL in yards per pass attempt at 5.6, improved to a 13-3 career record in games when he averages six yards per pass attempt or fewer, the best of all-time minimum 15 starts per CBS Sports Research, after averaging 4.0 yards per pass attempt on Thursday. All other active quarterbacks have a combined .283 winning percentage in starts where they average six yards per pass attempt or fewer. That's absolutely unfathomable. What other hijinks could take place across the rest of the NFL's Week 6 slate? Here is a look at five bold predictions. Packers run for over 100 yards for first time in 2026 vs. Cowboys The Green Bay Packers are back above .500 after quarterback Jordan Love's laser show (367 yards and 2 passing touchdowns while completing 25 of his 31 throws) in a 31-7 beatdown of the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field in Week 5. Now that they have a winning record, they're now the owners of the third-fewest rushing yards per game (60.4) by any team above .500 through five games of a season in league history, per CBS Sports Research. Green Bay's NFL-worst rushing offense also ranks as the fewest rushing yards per game through games of any season in the Packers' 106-season franchise history. Some of that has to do with the absence of running back Josh Jacobs , who is on the commissioner's exempt list after being charged with two misdemeanors, and some of that has to do with the team's beat-up offensive line. However, the offensive line has stabilized with veterans Laken Tomlinson and Travis Glover stabilizing the team's guard play. That's one of the reasons why the Packers will run for over 100 yards as a team for the first time in 2026 against the Dallas Cowboys on "Sunday Night Football." The others are that Green Bay running back MarShawn Lloyd is a freight train at 5 feet 9 inches tall and 220 pounds, and the Cowboys have the league's worst run defense (168.4 rushing yards allowed per game). Dallas allowed the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to go off for 241 yards rushing, their most in a game since 2024, on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 5. Facing a leaky defense like that and Lloyd fresh off running through Bears cornerback Jaylon Johnson's face for a touchdown in Week 5, Lloyd and the Packers cross the century mark on the ground for the first time this season. Marshawn Lloyd trucks a guy on his way to the end zone 😤 @CHIvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/NNcSwQfTOU Marvin Harrison Jr. has first 100-yard receiving game since his rookie year Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud is quietly playing efficient football: he has the fifth-most passing attempts without an interception (185) through five games in NFL history while throwing for the fourth-most passing yards in the NFL (1,402) this season. The Texans (1-4) have a high-volume passing offense this season because of their struggling rushing offense, and that will lead to Houston's newest player, 2024 fourth overall pick wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. , thriving in his team debut against the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars (4-1). How much will he soar in his first game back with his former Ohio State Buckeyes teammate in Stroud? Harrison Jr. will produce his first 100-yard receiving game since his rookie year in 2024 and just the third overall 100-yard receiving game of his young career on Sunday. He and Stroud were Ohio State teammates for two seasons from 2021 to 2022, and Harrison Jr.'s 14 receiving touchdowns when Stroud was the starting quarterback in 2022 are tied for the third most in a single season in Buckeyes' history. Harrison Jr. also set or tied career-highs in catches (77), receiving yards (1,263) and receiving touchdowns (14) in that 2022 season with Stroud. Houston will be celebrating their newest trade acquisition's 100-yard game when the clock hits zero at Wembley Stadium on Sunday. Justin Herbert ends fourth-quarter turnover streak and multi-passing touchdown drought vs. Chiefs The Los Angeles Chargers are injury-plagued and riding the struggle bus at 0-5 to start 2026. Pro Bowl quarterback Justin Herbert is tied for the most interceptions (seven) and turnovers (nine) in the NFL this season, and he has a couple of ugly streaks going against him. He has five consecutive games with a fourth-quarter turnover, making him the first quarterback since Charlie Frye in 2006 to do that. Herbert also hasn't thrown for multiple passing touchdowns in a game in his last seven games, the longest such streak of his career. However, he will play a clean fourth quarter and throw multiple touchdown passes against the 4-0 Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead on Sunday. The last time the Chiefs were on the field in Week 4, 38-year-old Kirk Cousins threw for 365 yards, 2 touchdowns and an interception on 31 of 52 passes in a narrow 30-27 Chiefs win. Herbert will snap out of his funk and raise his level to go toe-to-toe with Mahomes by having a clean fourth quarter and throwing multiple touchdowns for the first time in a while. Jets' Geno Smith throws first interception of 2026 at Patriots Geno Smith is on an incredible public relations campaign in 2026 with the New York Jets . After leading the NFL with 17 interceptions as a Las Vegas Raider in 2025, he hasn't thrown any through five games this season. Smith has six passing touchdowns to no interceptions this season, a stark contrast from his touchdown-to-interception ratio at this time a year ago when he had the same number of touchdown passes (six) but with nine interceptions. He is only the second quarterback in NFL history with no interceptions through five starts, after leading the league in interceptions the previous season, and is tied with Vinny Testaverde, also with the Jets, back in 2001, per CBS Sports Research. However, Smith will throw his first interception of the season in Week 6 at the New England Patriots . Patriots All-Pro cornerback Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) is on track to return this week, fully practicing on Thursday after being limited on Wednesday. In his first game back after a two-game absence, Gonzalez will intercept Smith for the veteran's first interception of 2026. Saints won't cover as road favorite at Giants Yes, your eyes don't deceive you. According to DraftKings Sportsbook , the 1-4 New Orleans Saints are favored by 1.5 points over the 3-1-1 New York Giants on the road at MetLife Stadium. Perhaps the ugliness of the NFC East leader's 27-27 tie at the Washington Commanders in Week 5 is pushing the spread in favor of the Saints. Maybe it's the allure of New Orleans quarterback Tyler Shough , whose 1,299 passing yards rank as the seventh-most in the NFL. Regardless, that positions the Saints to win on Sunday, as they have covered in seven consecutive road games, the longest active road cover streak in the entire NFL, per CBS Sports Research. However, the Saints' road cover streak will be broken on Sunday because Jameis Winston plays a more efficient brand of football than Shough. Sure, Winston's 57.6% is the second-worst in the NFL among 31 qualified quarterbacks in 2026, but he is starting to turn a corner and find a groove as an NFL starting quarterback once again. He is the first Giants quarterback with three-plus passing touchdowns in consecutive games since Eli Manning in 2016, and Winston didn't throw a single interception after having two in Week 4 against the Arizona Cardinals a couple of weeks ago. On the other hand, Shough has a turnover problem: his eight this season are the third-most in the league. The Cowboys fell victim to the trap game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Dallas was heavily favored, and rightly so, as Tampa Bay was 0-4 and starting an undrafted rookie quarterback. But Dallas failed to so much as show up and fell to 2-3 on the year. The Packers, on the other hand, absolutely throttled the Chicago Bears in what was far and away Green Bay's best game on both sides of the ball. Now, all of the talk of the Packers' demise has been shelved. These two teams squared off last season and battled to a 40-40 tie. Before that, Green Bay had beaten Dallas in eight of their last nine meetings. Will the Packers continue their dominance over the Cowboys? Or will Dallas flip the script and pull out a win? Here's what experts from different media outlets think. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Packers: 26 The biggest problem for the Cowboys in this game is Green Bay's ability to move the ball through the air . The Packers had struggled offensively over the first four contests, but they found their rhythm in Week 5 by torching the Bears with the deep ball. Defending the pass has been a major issue for the Cowboys this season, with Dallas ranking 21st. That doesn't even do justice for how bad it has really been. The Cowboys' ranking would be even worse if teams weren't abusing Christian Parker's unit on the ground. The good news for the Cowboys is the Packers haven't been able to run the football with any semblance of success, although Dallas presents a perfect get-right opportunity with their league-worst showing against the run this season. Green Bay has also struggled to stop the run, ranking 24th, but the Cowboys aren't running the ball like they did last season and it remains to be seen if they can capitalize on Green Bay's woes. Another problem for the Cowboys is the Packers are giving up the fifth-fewest yards per game through the air and if that holds true this week and the run game doesn't get on track, it's going to be tough sledding for Dallas' offense. Joey Porter Jr.'s return is going to make a dent in Dallas' passing game struggles, but the Cowboys still have the other side of the field to defend and DaRon Bland has proven incapable of doing that. The slot is a another concern if Caleb Downs is still playing most or all of his snaps at safety like he has amid the Cowboys' slew of injuries at safety. The Cowboys will get their points to keep this game close, but we're highly skeptical Dallas' secondary and pass-rush will do enough to keep Green Bay's passing attack at bay enough to emerge victorious. away.headline: NFL punishes 2 Dallas Cowboys players, capping off a bad week
away.blurb: Now, to add insult to injury, the NFL is punishing two Cowboys players for their actions in Week 4 of the NFL season. Every weekend, the NFL sends out a report with its weekly punishments for holding players accountable for their actions during the prior week's games . NFL punishes 2 Dallas Cowboys players, capping off a bad week - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL NFL punishes 2 Dallas Cowboys players, capping off a bad week Anne Erickson Sat, October 10, 2026 at 9:33 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Dallas Cowboys fell 24-16 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on "Thursday Night Football" to kick off the NFL's Week 5 festivities, and it wasn't a good look for the franchise. The main reason this loss was rough is because the Cowboys fell to a 0-4 Buccaneers team that has undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels subbing for the injured Baker Mayfield. You know something is wrong when you're losing to an undrafted free agent, but in all seriousness, Daniels was impressive. So, it could be more about his impressive showing than the Cowboys tanking, but still, this franchise is already on the clock to turn things around this season. Two Cowboys players fined by the NFL "Player infractions may come to the league's attention in a variety of ways. The league may respond to an official's call during a game or to a specific play that a team submits for review," the league notes. In this weekend's report, the NFL slaps Cowboys player Reddy Steward with a $5,583 fine for unnecessary roughness due to a hit on a defenseless player at 10:57 in the third quarter, as well as Kavontae Turpin with an $11,941 fine for unsportsmanlike conduct due to taunting at 10:50 in the third quarter. So, it's just a bit more bad news for two guys playing for a franchise that's hurting. But it's still early in the season, so the Cowboys have lots of time to come back. away.headline: Four players questionable, two out for Dallas Cowboys; will Micah Parsons play?
away.blurb: Cornerback Cobie Durant will miss his fourth consecutive game and backup offensive tackle Drew Shelton will miss a second consecutive game with hamstring injuries, as both were ruled out on Friday. Even though head coach Brian Schottenheimer said on Friday that linebacker DeMarvion Overshown is a “long shot” to play with a hamstring injury of his own, he was officially listed as questionable after logging limited participation in back-to-back practices this week. He has missed four games since suffering the injury in Week 1. Trade acquisition cornerback Joey Porter Jr. has been battling an ankle injury that limited him in practice on Wednesday and Friday. He was a full participant on Thursday. Fellow cornerback Ameer Speed has been battling a knee issue this week, but he was able to log back-to-back limited practices to finish the week. Both are officially listed as questionable. Rotational rookie defensive tackle LT Overton popped up on the injury report on Friday with a foot injury that prevented him from practicing. He is also listed as questionable. A quartet of players will not play for the Packers on Sunday night, as defensive tackle Jonathan Ford (calf), defensive tackle Javon Hargrave (achilles), wide receiver Skyy Moore (ankle) and cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring) were all ruled out on Friday. Defensive tackle Jordon Riley is working his way off the injured reserve list with an achilles injury, but he was ruled doubtful to be activated ahead of Sunday night. Five more players were listed as questionable, as defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle), rookie cornerback Brandon Cisse (hip), interior offensive lineman Jacob Monk (quad), guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe) and wide receiver Savion Williams (ankle) will all be gametime decisions. Williams will need to be activated off injured reserve on Saturday to have a shot at playing. While the Micah Parsons return was something that was certainly on the table when this game was scheduled back in May, the five-time Pro Bowler has yet to return to practice as he continues to heal from a torn ACL he suffered last December. He will not be activated in time for Sunday night’s game and will instead be watching his current and former team square off from the sideline. He is expected to return in early November. Four additional players were listed on the injury report this week but do not carry a designation into Sunday night: cornerback Keisean Nixon (groin), edge Lukas Van Ness (shoulder), safety Evan Williams (illness) and defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt (ankle). home.headline: Packers get Josh Jacobs boost as Micah Parsons faces longer injury absence
home.blurb: The Green Bay Packers are preparing for a major change to their backfield, with Josh Jacobs set to return as the team’s starting running back for their Week 7 matchup against the Detroit Lions. After missing the first part of the 2026 NFL season, Jacobs is expected to immediately reclaim his role when Green Bay travels to Detroit, giving the offense an important boost for the second half of the campaign. However, the Packers also received a less encouraging update regarding Micah Parsons . The star pass rusher remains unable to practice as he continues working toward a return from his knee injury, putting his availability for the upcoming games in doubt. His recovery timeline could keep him sidelined for several more weeks. NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported both developments. “Josh Jacobs will immediately return as the Packers’ starting running back next week at Detroit. Meanwhile, Micah Parsons still isn’t ready to practice, making it unlikely he plays before Nov. 8 against the Patriots at the soonest.” When will Josh Jacobs and Micah Parsons return for the Packers? Josh Jacobs is expected to step straight back into the starting role against Detroit after being removed from the NFL Commissioner Exempt List. His return comes at a time when Green Bay is looking to strengthen its running game, and the team’s decision to make him the starter immediately signals that the Packers expect him to resume his central role in the offense. Parsons, meanwhile, faces a longer wait before he can return to the field. Although he has been working toward recovery from reconstructive knee surgery, he has not yet received the clearance needed to resume practice . Until he is able to return to the practice field and build up his football activity, the Packers cannot count on him being available for a game. According to Pelissero’s report, November 8 against the New England Patriots is the earliest realistic possibility for Parsons to play, meaning he is unlikely to return before then. Green Bay will therefore have Jacobs back in the lineup while continuing to wait for one of its most important defensive players to complete his recovery. Josh Jacobs will return as Green Bay’s starting running back against Detroit. November 8 against the Patriots is the earliest Parsons could return. home.headline: NFL releases major update on status of Packers RB Josh Jacobs
home.blurb: The NFL removed Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs from the Commissioner Exempt List, effective Monday, making him eligible to return to the field for Sunday’s Week 7 matchup against the division-rival Detroit Lions. While Jacobs is now eligible to return to the roster, the NFL’s investigation under the league’s Personal Conduct Policy is still underway. Jacobs, who was arrested in May following a domestic disturbance, was originally placed on the Commissioner Exempt List before the 2026 season on Aug. 30. The NFL released a public statement following this move: “The National Football League today notified Josh Jacobs of the Green Bay Packers that he will be removed from the Commissioner Exempt List on Oct. 19. He will be eligible to play in the Packers’ Week 7 game on Oct. 25 after missing six games. “The NFL initiated an investigation under the Personal Conduct Policy following Jacobs’ arrest in May. The league’s review remains ongoing and is not affected by this change to Jacobs’ roster status.” Without Jacobs through the first five games of the 2026 season, the Packers rank dead last in rushing yards per game with 60.4. MarShawn Lloyd has just 112 rushing yards on the season, followed by Kaleb Johnson with 106. The Packers will face off against the Dallas Cowboys in a primetime “Sunday Night Football” matchup in Week 6. Brown coming off IR ALCS Game 4 postponed Defense will win WNBA Finals 49ers vs. Commanders Preview: San Francisco Looks to Stay Undefeated Photo by: Darren Yamashita Stephan Stroud Fri, October 16, 2026 at 8:53 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads 49ers Aim to Keep Rolling on Monday Night The San Francisco 49ers return home Monday night looking to extend their undefeated start when they host the Washington Commanders at Levi's Stadium. San Francisco enters the Week 6 matchup at 5-0 after an exciting 32-29 road victory over the Seattle Seahawks, while Washington arrives at 1-3-1 following a frustrating 27-27 overtime tie against the New York Giants. The matchup presents two teams heading in different directions. The 49ers have found ways to win close games, while the Commanders are searching for consistency as they attempt to climb back into the NFC playoff conversation. Kickoff is scheduled for 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN and ABC. Brock Purdy Leads San Francisco's Offense Quarterback Brock Purdy has helped guide the 49ers through an impressive opening stretch. Although San Francisco has faced several challenging opponents, the offense has continued producing at important moments. Purdy threw two touchdown passes against Seattle and helped lead the game-winning drive that set up Eddy Piñeiro's decisive field goal. His ability to distribute the football and make smart decisions has been important to the team's success. Running back Christian McCaffrey remains another major weapon. His versatility as both a runner and receiver gives head coach Kyle Shanahan several ways to attack opposing defenses. San Francisco will look to establish its running game early, create favorable passing situations and control the tempo. The 49ers' offense has also benefited from contributions across the roster, allowing the team to remain productive even when individual drives become difficult. Jayden Daniels Looks to Spark Washington Washington will rely on quarterback Jayden Daniels to help generate offense against a San Francisco defense that has started the season strongly. Daniels demonstrated his playmaking ability against the Giants, rushing for 103 yards and two touchdowns while throwing for 199 yards. However, Washington's inability to finish the game left the team with a disappointing tie. Daniels' mobility could be one of the Commanders' biggest advantages. San Francisco will need disciplined defensive play to prevent him from escaping the pocket and creating explosive gains with his legs. Washington also needs better protection up front and more consistent execution on third downs. Sustaining drives will be particularly important against a 49ers team that has repeatedly capitalized on scoring opportunities. Kyle Shanahan vs. Dan Quinn The coaching matchup adds another layer to Monday night's game. Shanahan has San Francisco playing confident football, while Quinn needs Washington to respond after letting a potential victory slip away. For the Commanders, limiting turnovers and improving their second-half execution will be essential. The 49ers, meanwhile, will look to continue their balanced offensive approach and use their home-field advantage. A Major Test for Both Teams San Francisco has an opportunity to improve to 6-0 and strengthen its position in the NFC West. Washington needs a complete performance to show it can compete with one of the conference's unbeaten teams. With Purdy and McCaffrey leading the 49ers against Daniels and Washington's offense, Monday night's matchup offers an important test for both teams as the NFL season moves deeper into October.

away.blurb: Commanders Prepare for Return of NFL's ‘Next Great' Cornerback The Washington Commanders think they might have a special player in second-year cornerback Trey Amos. The problem is, Amos hasn't been available for quite some time. The Commanders are 1-3-1 and coming off an embarrassing 27-27 tie against the New York Giants , in which Washington let time run out instead of attempting a 41-yard field goal. "SECONDARY REINFORCEMENTS ARE HERE!" DC News Now's Alex Flume wrote on his official X account. " Nick Cross and Trey Amos were out getting involved at Commanders practice Wednesday. Dan Quinn said before practice that they are both expected to practice in full this week. Could be a massive boost for the Commanders pass defense this week." By all accounts, Amos has focused entirely on rehabbing his injury to return to the lineup — something that's taken considerably longer than anyone anticipated. "Dan Quinn said CB Trey Amos tweaked his ankle while in coverage on a deep ball to Terry McLaurin the other day," The Athletic's Nicki Jhabvala wrote on her official X account on August 10. "Quinn said he'll know more in a day or so about his timetable to return." Unlock the latest Heavy on Commanders news — direct to your inbox. Updated Oct 16, 2026 at 11:27pm Amos has missed 12 consecutive regular-season games since Week 10 of his rookie season, when he fractured his fibula against the Detroit Lions . Now, when the Commanders may need him most, Amos looks like he'll be back and will make his comeback in a Week 6 primetime showdown against the unbeaten San Francisco 49ers on Monday Night Football. Play Trey Amos: Total Focus on Returning to Commanders "Trey Amos has no hobbies," Commanders reporter Ben Standig wrote on his official X account. "No distractions. Just football. After 11 months and two injuries, the Commanders CB wants his life back." Amos was coming into his own when he got injured — he made 8 starts in 10 games as a rookie. The Commanders have had one glaring weakness on their defense this season and it's been with 3r-dyear cornerback Mike Sainristil . Getting Amos back and healthy could put Amos, Amik Robertson , and Rasul Douglas at two outside cornerback spots and one slot cornerback spot. That would be the best-case scenario — mainly because it keeps Sainristil off the field. "My big question for MNF, assuming Trey Amos can play: is Amik going back to nickel? Or is he playing outside until it's nickel package and then sliding inside? Amik's been stellar outside, but Trey and Rasul are two of your three best corners, and neither are playing inside," The Full Command Show wrote on its official X account. Stefon Diggs, Jacory Croskey-Merritt, and Marcus Mariota did not practice as Washington got ready for its Monday Night Football matchup with San Francisco. Running back Austin Ekeler (chest), receiver Treylon Burks (shoulder), linebacker Jordan Magee (hamstring), safety Quan Martin (illness), cornerback Fabian Moreau (knee) and safety Jeremy Reaves (rib) were also limited. By Michael Gallagher Sports Content Coordinator 0 Share Newsweek is a Trust Project member See more of our trusted coverage when you search. Prefer Newsweek on Google to see more of our trusted coverage when you search. The San Francisco 49ers have had arguably the worst injury luck of any team in the NFL this season. More than 15 players are currently on the reserve/injured list while a handful of others are expected to miss some time with their respective ailments. San Francisco’s defense has been hit particularly hard, and star edge-rusher Nick Bosa’s absence over the last few weeks has been noticeable. Keion White has done his part to pick up the slack, but the rest of San Francisco’s pass-rush has left much to be desired, which is why Kristopher Knox of Bleacher Report believes the 49ers should make an all-in move to upgrade the position. Knox recently suggested the 49ers execute a trade with the winless Los Angeles Chargers for Pro Bowler Khalil Mack. “Los Angeles fell to 0-5 on Sunday, while Mack continues to be a legitimate difference-maker,” Knox wrote . “… Mack is playing on a one-year deal and should be interested in playing for a team that could get him his first career playoff win. “.. Mack should be the top target for any team with Super Bowl aspirations that happens to need help rushing opposing passers. It'll be a fairly significant surprise if he remains in Los Angeles beyond next month's deadline.” Despite multiple reports indicating the Chargers would want a fifth-round pick in exchange for Mack, Knox suggested it could take at least a conditional 2027 fourth-round pick to get a deal finalized given the demand for strong pass-rushers from contending teams. Through five games this season, Mack has logged 14 pressures, eight hurries, five tackles for loss, three QB hits, and three sacks with a pass-rush win-rate of 9.5%, according to Pro Football Focus. Adding that kind of production opposite White would be a big boost for the 49ers in the interim, and once Bosa comes back, it would make SF’s pass-rush all the more dangerous come playoff time.
